title: 辩论：人是怎么一步步走到当初绝不会做的事的？
title_en: How do people end up, step by step, doing what they once never would?

questions.question: 费斯廷格 1959 年的实验里，拿 1 美元去说「枯燥任务很有趣」的人，事后真觉得任务更有趣了。他据此提醒人们要提防什么？
options: 枯燥的工作：长期做重复无聊的事，会让人慢慢麻木、不知不觉地降低自己的标准
小诱惑：它小到不够当理由，你只好替自己编一个，而编出的理由会变成新信念
当众表态：一旦当着别人说出了口，人就会为了面子坚持到底、不再改口
大诱惑：给的钱越多，人越容易被收买，从而彻底改变自己原来的信念
questions.explanation: 拿 20 美元的人知道自己是为了钱，所以不必改信念；拿 1 美元的人没有足够的外部理由，只好改写信念来消除失调。费斯廷格的结论是「要提防的是小诱惑，不是大诱惑」，因为大贿赂你认得出。
questions.question_en: In Festinger's 1959 study, people paid $1 to say a boring task was fun later actually rated it as more enjoyable. What does he warn us to watch out for?
options_en: Boring work: doing repetitive tasks for long makes people numb and gradually lower their standards
Small temptations: too small to justify the act, so you invent a reason yourself, and that reason becomes a new belief
Public statements: once you've said something in front of others, pride makes you stick to it for good
Large temptations: the more money offered, the more easily people are bought and completely change their beliefs
questions.explanation_en: Those paid $20 knew they did it for the money, so they didn't need to change their beliefs; those paid $1 lacked an external justification and rewrote their beliefs to relieve the dissonance. Festinger's conclusion is to watch for small temptations rather than big ones, because a big bribe is easy to recognise.

questions.question: 沙罗特的实验显示，同样的谎重复下去，杏仁核反应一次比一次弱，谎也越撒越大。她据此给出的关键提醒是什么？
options: 别靠当下「这不对」的感觉判断，被调低的正是它；要趁早写下具体底线
杏仁核反应减弱说明撒谎的人天生缺少良知，这和他们所处的环境没有多大关系
只要心里的警报还在响就说明问题不大，等它真正消失了再停下来也还来得及
这种习惯化一旦形成就不可逆转，只能依靠药物把大脑的警觉重新提高上去
questions.explanation: 沙罗特说撒第十次谎的人主观上已不觉得在做坏事，所以「不能靠当下的感觉来判断」，建议趁还觉得不对时把底线写下来，日后对照纸而不是对照感觉。她也说习惯化可以被打断，换环境、离开一阵或有人点破都能去习惯化，所以「不可逆」不对。
questions.question_en: Sharot's study showed the amygdala responding less each time the same lie was repeated, while the lies grew bigger. What is her key takeaway?
options_en: Don't judge by the in-the-moment sense that 'this is wrong', since that is what gets turned down; write concrete limits down early
A fading amygdala response means liars are simply born without a conscience, regardless of their circumstances
As long as the inner alarm is still sounding things are fine, and stopping once it fades is still early enough
Once this habituation sets in it can't be reversed, and only medication can restore the brain's alertness
questions.explanation_en: Sharot says that by the tenth lie people no longer feel they're doing wrong, so you 'can't rely on present feelings', and she advises writing your limits down while they still feel wrong, so you later check against the paper rather than your gut. She also says habituation can be broken by a change of setting, time away, or someone pointing it out, so 'irreversible' is wrong.

questions.question: 埃德蒙森用哥伦比亚号失事前的泡沫块撞击来说明「偏差正常化」。它的核心机制是什么？
options: 每一次侥幸平安返航都被记成安全的证据，危险异常就慢慢变成了例行的维护问题
工程师故意隐瞒了泡沫撞击的数据，管理层因此从头到尾完全不知道发生过这种情况
安全规则定得过于严格，团队为了按期发射，只好想办法绕开整套流程
泡沫撞击在那次任务中是第一次出现，团队缺乏经验，因此低估了它的风险
questions.explanation: 泡沫脱落撞击机身已发生过多次，每次都平安返航，于是它从「危险异常」变成了「维护问题」，用她的话说，每一次侥幸都被记成了安全的证据。说它是「第一次出现」恰好错过了要点：正是反复发生、反复没事，才让标准被悄悄调低。
questions.question_en: Edmondson uses the foam strikes before the Columbia disaster to illustrate the 'normalisation of deviance'. What is the core mechanism?
options_en: Each lucky safe return was logged as evidence of safety, so a dangerous anomaly slowly became a routine maintenance issue
Engineers deliberately hid the foam-strike data, so management had no idea such strikes had ever happened
The safety rules were so strict that the team worked around the whole process to launch on schedule
The foam strike was a first-time event on that mission, and the inexperienced team underestimated the risk
questions.explanation_en: Foam had struck the orbiter many times and each flight returned safely, so it shifted from 'dangerous anomaly' to 'maintenance issue'; in her words, every near miss was recorded as proof of safety. Calling it a first-time event misses the point: it was the repeated, uneventful recurrence that quietly lowered the standard.
